claims.name: Continuous polling loop
claims.statement: All input handling (knobs, buttons, incoming MIDI) is driven from one unbounded while-True loop that calls monitor() on every component every iteration, rather than interrupts or callbacks.

rules: Every component exposes a parameterless monitor() method.
monitor() must return quickly and never block, since it shares one loop with every other component.
attrs.implementation: main.py's while True loop, calling monitor() on each of MidiKnob x2, MidiButton x2, VolumeLED

claims.name: Change-only MIDI emission
claims.statement: Both the knob and button components track their last-sent value and only emit a MIDI message when the current reading differs from it, avoiding a flood of identical messages.

rules: A knob only sends when the change exceeds potentiometerSensitivity (jitter guard).
A button only sends on an actual state transition, never on a steady state.
attrs.implementation: MidiKnob.potentiometerLastValue and MidiButton.lastState, compared each monitor() call

claims.name: Fixed MIDI channel/CC mapping
claims.statement: Every physical control is wired to one hardcoded MIDI channel and CC/note number, matched on the Mixxx side by a static XML mapping file rather than any runtime negotiation or MIDI-learn logic in code.

rules: A physical control's MIDI address is fixed at construction time in main.py and must be mirrored exactly in DJMixer.midi.xml.
Changing one side without the other silently breaks that control.

claims.name: Use CircuitPython on Raspberry Pi Pico as the controller platform
claims.statement: The hardware controller runs CircuitPython firmware on a Pico rather than a pre-built commercial MIDI controller or a different microcontroller stack.

attrs.context: Building a custom DJ mixer controller from raw components (potentiometers, buttons, LEDs)
consequences: Full control over pin mapping and MIDI behaviour
Firmware install and updates are entirely manual (see RUN-007)

claims.name: Bridge to Mixxx via a MIDI mapping script rather than a native plugin
claims.statement: Integration with Mixxx is done through its documented MIDI controller-scripting mechanism (a JS file plus an XML mapping) rather than a native/compiled Mixxx plugin.

attrs.context: Mixxx exposes a scripting API for third-party controllers; this is the standard, supported integration path
consequences: Integration is limited to whatever the MIDI scripting API exposes
